Registration for International Research Competition on Non-Terrestrial Networks

The Communications, Space and Technology Commission (CST), in partnership with the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE), is organizing the 3rd International Research Competition on Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN) 2026. The competition invites researchers, graduate students, and recent PhD graduates from around the world to submit innovative research on non-terrestrial networks, future wireless communications, and the integration of terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks. Selected finalists will present their research during the Global Space Connectivity and Sustainability Events in Riyadh, where the winners will be announced. The competition aims to promote research and innovation in next-generation connectivity technologies and strengthen international collaboration in developing sustainable communications solutions. Echoes of the Familiar

Echoes of the Familiar exhibition explores the concept that home transcends mere physical space, embodying a tapestry of memories intricately woven into its very walls. It is within these confines that the echoes of laughter from childhood games intermingle with the remnants of disagreements and tears shed upon pillows. Each drawer brims with knick-knacks whose purposes remain elusive yet evoke nostalgia. The scent of maternal cooking and the rhythmic snoring of a father create a comforting ambiance, while the presence of a grandmother before the television grounds us in familial continuity. Tafasahu: Make Room

Tafasahu: Make Room is an exhibition that showcases a commissioned installation by Saudi architect and artist, Nada AlMulla, which invites you to enter as a guest&mdash;to pause, gather and reflect on the conditions of belonging within the context of the traditional Majlis, Arabic for "gathering space." Beyond being a place to receive and host guests, the Majlis has been a vessel for the transmission of knowledge and heritage. The installation deconstructs this space into its essential elements while centering stories, memories and subtle traces of everyday life that animated it: conversations shared over coffee, the lingering scent of incense, the rhythms of gathering and departure. Beaded plant Suncatcher

Sunlight has a way of bringing a space to life. As it passes through a window, it fills a room with color, movement, and small moments that make a house feel like home. In this workshop, participants create beaded plant sun catchers inspired by the light that streams through our windows and the natural elements we welcome into our homes. By combining colorful beads and delicate forms, each piece is designed to catch and reflect sunlight, creating shifting patterns of color and light. The result is a decorative artwork that celebrates the warmth of home through nature, color, and light.

Ajeeb in Wonder House

A story-led experience that follows Ajeeb as he visits a series of unusual homes, each shaped by a different idea, form, or function. As the story unfolds, children observe how each space reflects a way of living, then shift into designing a home that suits Ajeeb himself. The activity combines storytelling with creative decision-making, moving from observation to design.

The Saudi Food Show

The Saudi Food Show returns to Riyadh Front Exhibition & Convention Center, bringing together global food and beverage leaders to showcase the latest trends, products, and innovations shaping the Kingdom’s fast-growing F&B sector. Alongside the exhibition floor, the Elite Lounge serves as the heart of the Tawasul Meetings—a premium space where top buyers meet top brands and conversations turn into real business impact. Visitors can also catch the excitement at Top Table Saudi, featuring chef-led masterclasses, bold flavours, and standout culinary moments from global icons and local talent, while the Saudi Food Summit delivers interactive sessions on everything from branding strategy to industrial incentives, helping shape the future of F&B. For coffee lovers, Coffee World adds another layer of energy with hands-on masterclasses blending flavour, technique, and passion. Book Now

The Art of Islamic Illumination

This 5-day course will take art lovers, painters, calligraphers and traditional art enthusiasts on an engaging journey. This course is essential for participants who enjoy learning about Islamic floral shapes, which consist of stylized botanical forms of leaves and flowers&mdash;the foundation of traditional Islamic illumination. In this hands-on course, artists passionate about Islamic art will explore part of the history behind these shapes. They will learn and practice how to paint Islamic flowers on paper using gouache colors and shell gold. Desert X AlUla 2026

Returning for its fourth edition, Desert X AlUla 2026 explores Space Without Measure, inspired by Kahlil Gibran’s meditations on possibility, perception and the boundless nature of the human spirit. Large-scale, site-specific installations by Saudi and international artists respond to AlUla’s unique landscape, history, and culture. A vibrant programme of tours and events invites deeper engagement, continuing to build AlUla’s legacy as a global destination for art in the landscape. Desert X can be enjoyed in a variety of ways, including on foot - self-guided, or as part of a public or private guided tour - or in the comfort of an open-top car.
